title: Semicontinuity and base change
statement:
Let $f:X\to T$ be a proper morphism of finite presentation and $\cF$ an
$\cO_X$-module of finite presentation, flat over $T$. For every integer
$q$ the function
$t\mapsto\dim_{\kappa(t)}H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$ is upper semicontinuous on
$T$, and there are canonical base-change maps
$R^qf_*\cF\otimes\kappa(t)\to H^q(X_t,\cF_t)$, defined through the
Čech complexes of a finite affine cover over an affine open
neighbourhood of $t$. If moreover $T$ is
*reduced* and this function is locally constant, then $R^qf_*\cF$ is
finite locally free (in particular flat), and if $T$ is moreover locally
Noetherian, the base-change maps in degree $q$ are isomorphisms.

proof.text: Fix $q\in\mathbf Z$. Apply [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] with the given proper finitely presented $f$ and finitely presented $\mathcal F=\cF$ flat over $T$. Its fibres $X_t=X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ and $\mathcal F_t$ are exactly ours. Clauses (1) and (2) give finite-dimensional fibre cohomology, canonical maps $\varphi^q(t)$ and upper semicontinuity of the displayed dimension function. This reuses the existing finite-free-model/rank-minor theorem rather than introducing a second semicontinuity theorem.

source.place: First paragraph: finite-free model, rank semicontinuity and reduced-base local freeness; second paragraph: canonical Cech map

proof.text: To specify these canonical maps by the requested Cech construction, work over an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$. The restricted morphism is separated and quasi-compact (properness includes these properties), and $\cF$ is quasi-coherent by the flat-over convention. For a finite affine cover of $X_V$, [lem-pc-cech-resolution] identifies its Cech complex $C$ with the derived direct image. Apply [lem-pc-base-change-map-cech] to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)\to V$: the canonical derived comparison is represented by the cochain map $\gamma:C\otimes_A\kappa(t)\to C_t$ whose components send $s\otimes b$ to $b\,p^*s$. On cohomology the ordinary comparison sends $[z]\otimes b$ to $[\gamma(z\otimes b)]$. This is well-defined: cycles map to cycles, a boundary $dw$ maps to $d\gamma(w\otimes b)$, and the formula is balanced and additive. The cited canonical-comparison equality identifies this with $\varphi^q(t)$, so it is independent of the chosen cover and affine neighbourhood. Thus these are precisely the Cech-defined maps in the item.

source.place: Second paragraph, first two sentences: definition through Cech complexes

proof.text: If $T$ is reduced and the degree-$q$ dimension function is locally constant, clause (3) of [thm-pc-semicontinuity-base-change] gives $R^qf_*\cF$ finite locally free, hence flat. For the isomorphism assertion assume also that $T$ is locally Noetherian. The isomorphism of the same canonical $\varphi^q(t)$ is given by clause (3) of the cited theorem in its present DAG form, and by clause (4) in the form recorded in its blueprint_update (current blueprint): there the hypotheses are $T$ reduced and locally Noetherian and $\beta^q(s)=\beta^q(t)$ for every generization $s$ of $t$, which holds because a generization of $t$ lies in every open neighbourhood of $t$, in particular in one on which $\beta^q$ is constant. Local constancy allows different ranks on different components; no global constant-rank hypothesis is imposed. The cited theorem is stated for every integer $q$ (the updated form for $q\ge0$; for $q<0$ both sides of every assertion are zero), so negative degrees as well as $q=0$ are included.

lean.statement: theorem picard_semicontinuity {X T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ T) [IsProper f] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsFinitePresentation] (hF : F.IsFlatOver f) [HasDerivedCategory.{wX} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] [HasDerivedCategory.{wT} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings T.toRingedSpace))] (q : ℤ) : UpperSemicontinuous (fun t : T ↦ if 0 ≤ q then F.hFiber f q.toNat t else 0) ∧ (IsReduced T → IsLocallyConstant (fun t : T ↦ if 0 ≤ q then F.hFiber f q.toNat t else 0) → SheafOfModules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.{u, u, u} ((schemeModuleHigherDirectImage f q).obj F) ∧ IsFlatOver (X := T) ((schemeModuleHigherDirectImage f q).obj F) (𝟙 T))
lean.note: The two new statements retain integer degrees, using zero fibre dimension in negative degrees, and the recorded integer-degree schemeModuleHigherDirectImage. The map clause reuses the public upstream cechBaseChangeMap from WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.Cohomology.DirectImage.BaseChangeMap, included in declarations rather than defined a second time. It is homology base change followed by the canonical Cech tensor comparison, over every affine neighbourhood and finite affine cover. The final theorem gives bijectivity of this same map under the reduced, locally constant and locally Noetherian hypotheses. Finite locally free has variable local rank; flatness is IsFlatOver of the identity. Reviewer fix: the two derived-category universes of X and T are bound separately (wX, wT), as in schemeModuleHigherDirectImage, instead of being tied to one w.
